chief_complaint: drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty chewing meat that worsens by evening
hpi_details: 4-month history of fluctuating, fatigable weakness affecting her eyelids, eye movements, and jaw muscles. Characteristically wakes up in the morning feeling entirely refreshed with normal vision, but as the afternoon progresses and especially while reading or driving home, both upper eyelids sag heavily (ptosis) and she experiences horizontal double vision (diplopia). While eating dinner, her jaw muscles become so exhausted after chewing tough meat that she has to hold her chin up with her hand to finish chewing. Also notes voice changing to nasal quality during long telephone calls at work. Denies limb numbness or pain.
ideas: thinks her eye muscles and jaw are suffering from severe muscular strain or chronic fatigue syndrome
concerns: worried her breathing or swallowing muscles will suddenly fail while eating dinner alone
expectations: wants specific antibody testing and nerve boosting tablets to restore her muscle strength throughout the day
pmh: hypothyroidism on thyroxine, no prior hospitalizations
social_hx: non-smoker, drinks socially, legal secretary, married

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Myasthenia Gravis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Initiate symptomatic acetylcholinesterase inhibitor therapy: pyridostigmine starting 30-60mg every 4-6 hours while awake (warn regarding cholinergic side effects: abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, salivation), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty chewing meat that worsens by evening

Key HPI features: 4-month history of fluctuating, fatigable weakness affecting her eyelids, eye movements, and jaw muscles. Characteristically wakes up in the morning feeling entirely refreshed with normal vision, but as the afternoon progresses and especially while reading or driving home, both upper eyelids sag heavily (ptosis) and she experiences horizontal double vision (diplopia). While eating dinner, her jaw muscles become so exhausted after chewing tough meat that she has to hold her chin up with her hand to finish chewing. Also notes voice changing to nasal quality during long telephone calls at work. Denies limb numbness or pain.

Objective/Exam findings: Perform bedside fatigue testing: sustained upward gaze for 60 seconds provokes progressive worsening bilateral ptosis and diplopia. Look for Cogan lid twitch on return to primary gaze. Bedside Ice Pack Test: placing an ice pack over the ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes may produce significant (>2 mm) improvement in eyelid elevation. Check bulbospinal power and neck flexion. Bloods: acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Ab positive in 85% of generalized MG; if negative, check anti-MuSK antibodies), thyroid function. Single-fiber electromyography (SFEMG - gold standard showing increased jitter and blocking) or repetitive nerve stimulation (decremental response >10% at 3 Hz). Contrast CT Thorax to screen for thymoma or thymic hyperplasia (present in up to 15% of AChR-positive patients).
Relevant background/PMH: hypothyroidism on thyroxine, no prior hospitalizations
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Myasthenia Gravis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (improves with exercise, associated with lung cancer) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Breathing or swallowing difficulty — signals myasthenic crisis, needing urgent ICU-level care.
management_principles: Initiate symptomatic acetylcholinesterase inhibitor therapy: pyridostigmine starting 30-60mg every 4-6 hours while awake (warn regarding cholinergic side effects: abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, salivation)
Refer to neurology for initiation of immunosuppression (oral prednisolone + azathioprine or mycophenolate) once diagnosis confirmed
Schedule elective thymectomy if thymoma found or in generalized AChR-positive patients aged <65
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 34F presents with fluctuating, fatigable ptosis, binocular diplopia, jaw claudication/weakness, and dysarthria worsening systematically toward the evening over 4 months.
reference_soap.objective: Perform bedside fatigue testing: sustained upward gaze for 60 seconds provokes progressive worsening bilateral ptosis and diplopia. Look for Cogan lid twitch on return to primary gaze. Bedside Ice Pack Test: placing an ice pack over the ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes may produce significant (>2 mm) improvement in eyelid elevation. Check bulbospinal power and neck flexion. Bloods: acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Ab positive in 85% of generalized MG; if negative, check anti-MuSK antibodies), thyroid function. Single-fiber electromyography (SFEMG - gold standard showing increased jitter and blocking) or repetitive nerve stimulation (decremental response >10% at 3 Hz). Contrast CT Thorax to screen for thymoma or thymic hyperplasia (present in up to 15% of AChR-positive patients).
reference_soap.assessment: Myasthenia Gravis (generalized fatigable autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder). DDx: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS - differentiated by proximal lower limb weakness that IMPROVES with exercise, dry mouth, associated with small cell lung cancer), ocular myositis, thyroid ophthalmopathy, intracranial aneurysm causing third nerve palsy.
reference_soap.plan: Initiate symptomatic acetylcholinesterase inhibitor therapy: pyridostigmine starting 30-60mg every 4-6 hours while awake (warn regarding cholinergic side effects: abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, salivation). Refer to neurology for initiation of immunosuppression (oral prednisolone + azathioprine or mycophenolate) once diagnosis confirmed. Schedule elective thymectomy if thymoma found or in generalized AChR-positive patients aged <65. Educate on myasthenic crisis warning signs (dyspnoea/dysphagia requiring urgent ICU admission and IVIG/plasmapheresis) and contra-indicated drugs (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, beta-blockers, magnesium).

learning_objectives: Elicit the cardinal clinical pattern of Myasthenia Gravis: fluctuating, fatigable weakness of ocular, bulbar, and proximal muscles with diurnal variation
Perform bedside diagnostic tests: sustained upward gaze fatigue test and the Ice Pack test
Explain the mandatory requirement of CT thorax screening to exclude thymoma in newly diagnosed myasthenics
List critical drugs contraindicated in Myasthenia Gravis (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, beta-blockers) that precipitate myasthenic crisis

teaching.one_liner: An autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction causes fatigable weakness that is normal in the morning and worsens through the day — drooping eyelids, double vision, and jaw fatigue while chewing — distinct from a fixed neurological deficit.
differentials: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (improves with exercise, associated with lung cancer)
Intracranial aneurysm causing third nerve palsy
red_flags: Breathing or swallowing difficulty — signals myasthenic crisis, needing urgent ICU-level care

must_ask.say: Do you feel fine in the morning, and does the drooping get worse as the day goes on?
Do your eyelids droop, or do you see double?
Does your jaw get tired chewing tough food, like meat?
Does your voice change or sound nasal during long conversations?

It started gradually about four months ago and has slowly gotten more noticeable over time.
Both of my upper eyelids droop, though my left eyelid usually sags a little lower than my right.
No, my vision has never blacked out or gone completely dark.
My actual eyesight is clear, but when my eyelids droop down they block the top of my view, and things split into two images side by side.
Both near reading and seeing far away become double once my eyes get tired, but my glasses prescription hasn't changed.
I don't have glare or halos around lights, but driving home at night is very tricky because of the double vision.
No, I haven't seen any floating specks, bright flashes, or dark curtains over my vision.
Yes, objects split side by side horizontally. If I cover either eye with my hand, the double image goes away immediately.
I wake up in the morning feeling completely refreshed with normal vision, but as the afternoon goes on my eyelids sag heavily and my vision splits.
When I eat dinner, my jaw muscles get so exhausted chewing meat that I have to hold my chin up with my hand to finish, though I haven't choked.
Yes, during long telephone calls at work, my voice gets tired and turns into a strange nasal sound.
I can breathe normally right now, but I worry constantly that my breathing muscles might suddenly get weak.
No, my eyes don't hurt, there is no pain when I look around, and they aren't red.
No, I don't have any new headaches, no tenderness around my temples, and my jaw gets tired from fatigue rather than pain.
I don't have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my arms or legs, and I don't feel dizzy.
No, I have never had any head injuries or trauma to my face or eyes.
No, I don't have high blood pressure or diabetes, and my last routine eye checkup was completely normal.
No, I don't have an irregular heartbeat, carotid artery issues, or any cardiovascular problems.
No, I don't have high myopia, glaucoma, or cataracts, and I've never had eye surgery.
No, I have never taken steroids, hydroxychloroquine, ethambutol, or any medicated eye drops.
No one in my family has glaucoma, macular degeneration, or unexplained vision problems.
Reading legal documents at work and driving home in the evening are very difficult because of the drooping and double vision, though I haven't fallen.
I have an underactive thyroid, which has been stable and well controlled for about three years.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I take levothyroxine 100 micrograms once every morning, and no other medications or supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications or foods.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink socially, maybe a single glass of wine on the weekend.
I work as a legal secretary, and I live with my husband.
My mother has mild high blood pressure, but there are no nerve disorders or autoimmune conditions in my family.
My periods come regularly every twenty-eight days, and my last period started two weeks ago.
We use barrier contraception, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Alert young female in no distress, resting her chin on her hand while conversing.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air, and temperature 36.7°C.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in each eye without pinhole correction, visual fields are full to confrontation, pupils are equal and reactive without afferent pupillary defect, and funduscopic examination shows clear media and sharp optic discs.

Sustained upward gaze for 60 seconds provokes progressive worsening bilateral ptosis and horizontal binocular diplopia with a positive Cogan lid twitch, both markedly improving after a two-minute ice pack test.
Both superficial temporal arteries are readily palpable, non-tender, and pulsatile without thickening or nodularity.
Neck flexion demonstrates mild fatigable weakness at grade 4/5, whereas proximal and distal limb power is fully preserved at grade 5/5 bilaterally.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are normal at 2+ bilaterally without post-exercise facilitation, and plantar responses are flexor.
Light touch and pinprick sensation are completely preserved and symmetric across the face and all four extremities.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth without palpable nodules or bruits.
